findings.source_quote: καὶ προφητειῶν ἀμαυρὰ καὶ ἀμφίβολα, ἵνα ἄλλου προφήτου χρείαν ἔχῃ τὰ λεγόμενα πρὸς ἐπίγνωσιν, ἀλλὰ ῥητὰ καὶ ἁπλᾶ
findings.english_quote: and, of prophecies, dim and ambiguous things, so that what is said should need another prophet for understanding, but explicit and plain things
findings.issue: Although the surviving wording is represented and the difficulty is openly disclosed, this English fragment supplies no defensible predication connecting the obscure and ambiguous things with the contrasting explicit and plain things. On the draft’s genitive interpretation of προφητειῶν, its syntactic connection also remains unexplained. The note’s conjectural καὶ οὐ προφητεύει introduces a predicate and an explicit negation absent from the supplied reading; it cannot establish the fidelity of the current translation. The block concerns unresolved clause meaning, not unverified print or merely the existence of alternative interpretations.
findings.suggested_revision: Provide a defensible grammatical and lexical construal of the exact image-checked wording, accounting for προφητειῶν, the neuter adjectives, the purpose clause, and ἀλλὰ without silently inserting a predicate or negation. Keep any textual conjecture explicitly separate from the selected reading. The print is already verified; the missing evidence is an adequately supported interpretation. Any resulting revised English requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ἵνα ἐφ᾽ ὧν ὁ λόγος ἐρρέθη, καὶ τὸ ἔργον γένηται
findings.english_quote: so that, in the matters about which the word was spoken, the deed might also occur
findings.issue: The draft chooses a neuter, topical interpretation of ἐφ᾽ ὧν without disclosing the material personal/temporal alternative: the deed occurs in the days of those in whose days the statement was spoken. That alternative is contextually significant after the prediction concerning this generation and the appeal to seeing events with one’s own eyes. The draft’s contextual rendering is defensible, but its note apparatus does not preserve this alternative or explain the choice.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note identifying the topical reading used in the main text and the personal/temporal alternative, explaining why the topical reading was chosen. A source-transparent formulation of the alternative is: “so that the deed too might occur in the days of those in whose days the word was spoken.” No source correction is required. Any change to the main rendering and its disclosure must undergo fresh review.
